texts.orig: 1 Introduction
texts.text: 1 Introduction

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Halverton Borough Council (the Council) invites tenders for a digital case management service for its housing repairs, licensing, complaints and environmental health teams. The service replaces systems that the Council has used since 2009, and it becomes the main tool for 350 staff who handle about 85,000 cases a year. The Council serves about 140,000 residents across eleven wards, and about sixty percent of new cases now start online.
texts.text: Halverton Borough Council (the Council) invites tenders for a digital case management service for its housing repairs, licensing, complaints and environmental health teams. The service replaces systems that the Council has used since 2009, and it becomes the main tool for 350 staff who handle about 85,000 cases a year. The Council serves about 140,000 residents across eleven wards, and about sixty percent of new cases now start online.

texts.orig: This request for proposal sets out the Council's needs, the procedure for this tender, the way tenders are evaluated and the main terms of the contract. The procurement follows the open procedure of the Halverton Public Contracts Rules 2025, under which any interested supplier can submit a tender. The contract runs for five years from 2027-04-01, with options to extend it twice by one year each.

texts.orig: 2 Background and current situation
texts.text: 2 Background and current situation

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Housing repairs are recorded in the Quillbeck housing records system, which also holds the Council's tenancy and property records. Licensing applications are held in the Pellworth licensing database, and complaints and environmental health requests are tracked in spreadsheets kept by each team. Scanned letters and forms since 2009 are kept in the Thornlea document archive. About 1.2 million historic case records are spread across these systems.
texts.text: Housing repairs are recorded in the Quillbeck housing records system, which also holds the Council's tenancy and property records. Licensing applications are held in the Pellworth licensing database, and complaints and environmental health requests are tracked in spreadsheets kept by each team. Scanned letters and forms since 2009 are kept in the Thornlea document archive. About 1.2 million historic case records are spread across these systems.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Council plans to replace the Quillbeck housing records system during 2028, and the replacement has not yet been procured.
texts.text: The Council plans to replace the Quillbeck housing records system during 2028, and the replacement has not yet been procured.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Staff enter the same resident details again in several systems, and no system shows a resident's cases across every team. Managers build the monthly performance reports by hand from exports, which takes about four working days each month. Residents who telephone the Council about a case are often told that an officer will call them back, because the contact center cannot see the case. In 2025 the contact center took about 61,000 calls about the status of existing cases, which is a third of all its calls.

texts.orig: An internal audit in 2025 found duplicate resident records in about eight percent of the Quillbeck data, and a project to cleanse the data has not yet started.

texts.orig: The current support contract for the Pellworth licensing database ends on 2027-12-31, and the Council does not plan to extend it. The spreadsheets of the complaints and environmental health teams are kept on a shared drive with no audit trail and no backup outside the Civic Center.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The digital strategy sets three aims for the new service: one record of each resident's cases, fewer calls about the status of a case, and reports that need no manual work. The Council measures the first aim by the share of cases linked to a single resident record, the second by the number of status calls each month, and the third by the hours spent on the monthly reports. A baseline for each measure was taken in 2025, and the service board reviews the measures each quarter after go-live.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Council reviewed its case handling in 2025 with the help of an external adviser. The review mapped 41 separate case processes across the four teams and found that 17 of them used paper forms at some stage. It also found that officers spent about a fifth of their time looking up information in other systems.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: A survey of 1,200 residents in 2025 found that two thirds wanted to follow their case online, and that the most common complaint was not knowing what happens next. A survey of staff found that most officers kept their own lists of cases outside the systems, to keep track of deadlines.
